context: Add a repository invariant test that runs the canonical detector over every results-data JSON file and fails on any leak, and wire it into a required CI lane so a violation cannot merge. Complements the one-time cleanup in results-explorer-curated-corpus-path-sanitization, whose scope forbids workflow changes.
description: The fail-closed privacy contract exists in scripts/validate_submission.py and benchbox/core/results/anonymization.py, but nothing scans the corpus as a whole, so pre-existing violations were never caught. Measured on develop 3af42e29b with the project's own find_public_path_leaks detector: 183 of 399 results-data JSON files fail, across execution.driver_runtime_python_executable, platform.config.working_dir, platform.raw_config.working_dir, platform.raw_metadata.driver_runtime_python_executable and platform.config.database_path. The identical 179 leaking bundles are present on the public published-results branch and have been public since 2026-05-13. Scope note verified 2026-08-03: this does NOT reach the Explorer's published output. Running AnonymizationManager over all 179 leaking bundles leaves zero leaks, and pipeline.py raises on any survivor, so the deployed site is insulated. This item is about preventing silent reaccumulation.

preserves.behavior: The canonical detector stays the single source of truth for both submission and explorer boundaries
The gate fails closed when a file cannot be parsed rather than skipping it
The gate scans every results-data JSON file, not only files changed in the PR
